This table contains information describing the vegetation communities that can be found in the study area (7.5 minute quad boundaries of La Mesa, La Jolla, Del Mar and Poway). This table is intended to be used as part of the Using ArcGIS geoprocessing tools Quick-start tutorial. The tutorial can be found in chapter 2 of "Using ArcGIS geoprocessing tools". Vegetation cover for the study area can be mapped by joining this table to the vegetation shapefile (vegtype.shp). The values in the Holland95 column in vegtable.dbf can be matched to the values in the Holland95 column in vegtype.shp. en

Documentation provided by the park did not indicate the origin of the habitat.dbf data, nor what type of habitat was being described. However, it was clear that land cover and vegetation were defined in that table. The landform shapefile provided by the Park (not used in the tutorial) was accompanied by documentation indicating that vertical aerial photography with near-infrared film was taken in late summer of 1982 and 1983. And, that stereo interpretive methods were used to interpret transpiring vegetation, exposed bedrock, and talus. Presumably this is one of the sources for the data in the habitat.dbf table. The original table provided by the Park was simplified for use with the ArcCatalog tutorial. Three columns, N12, N13, and N14, were removed because they were empty using ArcView 3.1. Also, the Integer column VegID was added to the table. Values were added to this column by calculating them to equal the values in the original Number column, which also contained Integer values. Then, the Number column was removed; this eliminated any ambiguity that might arise in the tutorial by referring to that column by name. (1999. Source: ynp\meta\habitat.dbf. Product: vegtype.dbf) The Primary column was added to the table using ArcView 3.1, then the table was edited. The purpose was to make it easier to illustrate sorting a table by multiple columns. The first species listed in the Name1 column was presumed to be the dominant species for each type of land cover; that species name was copied and pasted from the Name1 column to the Primary column. (1999.
